land.text: the Rhine land ceded to the Burgundian foederati near Worms

land.text: the whole kingdom: 'the rule of the Burgundian kings ended and the kingdom became part of Francia' in 534 (Kingdom page); 'definitively incorporated into their empire and finally divided among themselves in 534' (Godomar page)

successors.note: Burgundy returns as a Frankish sub-kingdom from 561 (Guntram) and under Theuderic II and Clovis II; Cliopatria's 602-660 shapes of this row are written as the separate dossier frankish-burgundy.

capitals.name: Borbetomagus (Worms)
capitals.note: Infobox: Borbetomagus 411-437; the kingdom of Gundahar on the Rhine. The state's land ends in about 436 (ledger).

capitals.name: Genava (Geneva)
capitals.note: Infobox: Genava 443-461; Godegisel held Geneva again after the 474 division and Sigismund ruled from Geneva from about 501.

capitals.name: Lugdunum (Lyon)
capitals.note: Infobox: Lugdunum 461-534; the body says the capital moved 'from Geneva to Lyon'. After 474 the brothers held Vienne (Chilperic II) and Valence (Godomar I) as seats.

rulers.name: Gundahar (Gunther)
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: Infobox 'Gunther 411-437'; the body names him Gundahar, granted land by Honorius in 411 and killed 'around 436' by Aetius with his Hun allies. The list starts at the state's start year.

rulers.name: Gundioc
rulers.note: First named in 456: 'In 456 the Burgundian kings Gundioc and Chilperic' campaign in Spain with the Visigoths (Kingdom page; also Hydatius via the Gundioc page); 'the first time that any of the royal family in Sapaudia are mentioned by name in contemporary records'. No page names a king between Gundahar's death (about 436) and 456. End: Gundobad page 'in either 473 or 474'; the Gundioc page adds c. 470 (Wolfram), before 467 (Kaiser) or late 474, 'little evidence'. 463: appointed magister militum (Gundioc page).

rulers.name: Chilperic I
rulers.title: co-ruler
rulers.note: Gundobad page infobox 'Chilperic I (473-c. 480)'; the Kingdom page has Chilperic repelling the Visigoths in 471 and dead by about 480.

rulers.name: Gundobad
rulers.note: King of the Burgundians from 473 to 516; principal king from about 480 (Kingdom page).

rulers.name: Godegisel
rulers.title: co-ruler
rulers.note: Held Geneva; allied with Clovis against Gundobad in 500; killed in Vienne in 501.

rulers.name: Sigismund
rulers.note: Ruled from Geneva from about 501; captured and executed in 523/524.

rulers.name: Godomar II
rulers.note: Infobox 524-534; his fate after the defeat near Autun is not known (Godomar page).

region.text: Gundahar's land on the western bank of the Rhine, probably near Worms

ledger.note: 413: the Burgundians become Roman foederati on the Rhine. After Honorius regained the Rhine region from Jovinus in 413 the Burgundians were accepted as Roman foederati; the infobox dates the grant of land to 411. The page places the settlement 'probably near Worms' and gives no boundary.

region.text: Gundahar's Rhine settlement near Worms, held as Roman federates

ledger.note: 413: the Burgundians are Roman federates on the Rhine. 'Gundahar's Burgundians were accepted as Roman foederati' (Kingdom page, after Honorius regained the Rhine region from Jovinus in 413). The page does not call them vassals; the federate status is read as the client tint, the model the western-roman-empire dossier uses (its 413 vassal_start and 436 vassal_end with counterpart burgundian-kingdom). Added after review eu-06-c.

About 436: Aetius ends the federation. 'In about 436, Gundahar and many of the people he led were killed by the Roman military leader Flavius Aetius' (Kingdom page). The Aetius page has the Burgundians defeated and obliged to accept peace by Aetius and Avitus in 436 and Hun foederati sent against them 'the following year'; the same pair as the western-roman-empire dossier's 436 vassal_end. Added after review eu-06-c.

About 436: Aetius and the Huns destroy the Rhine kingdom. Gundahar and many of the people he led were killed by the Roman military leader Flavius Aetius working with Hun allies; the infobox gives the Worms capital to 437. The land passes to the Roman side (Aetius) and the Huns; no page opened names the new holder. Second page (Flavius Aetius): 436 the Burgundians defeated and obliged to accept peace, 'the following year' (437) Hun foederati sent to destroy them, 443 the remnant settled in Sapaudia; the page does not say who held the Worms area afterwards (not settled).

region.text: Sapaudia: Geneva, Neuchâtel, Franche-Comté and the Saône valley

ledger.note: 443: the survivors are settled in Sapaudia. The Gallic Chronicle of 452: 'Sapaudia was given to the remainders of the Burgundians to be divided with the indigenous inhabitants'; the area included Geneva and Neuchâtel, in Maxima Sequania. The Sapaudia page adds the bounds: the Vosges, the Aar, the upper Rhône and the Saône valley. [Review eu-06-c: confidence 2, not 3. The region is Cliopatria's 443 shape, which reaches the Yonne and the Nievre (west to 2.95 E, about 60 cells west of 4.3 E); the Kingdom page names only Geneva and Neuchatel in Maxima Sequania, and the Sapaudia page gives the land around Lake Neuchatel bounded by the Vosges, the Aar, the upper Rhone and the Saone valley.]
443: the capital is Geneva (infobox 'Genava 443-461').

region.text: the Rhône valley: Isère, Drôme, Ardèche, Loire, Rhône and Savoie, 171 cells added in Cliopatria's 455 shape

ledger.note: 456: the Burgundians settle the Rhône valley. Marius of Avenches: 'occupied part of Gaul and divided the lands with the Gallic senators' (456); in 457 Gundioc 'entered Gaul to settle', with soldiers possibly garrisoned in Lyon. The page names 'part of Gaul', the region is Cliopatria's 455 addition.

region.text: Lyon and the Rhône valley taken by Majorian

ledger.note: 458: Majorian takes Lyon. Majorian occupied Lyon (Kingdom page); the Majorian page has him enter the Rhône valley in late 458, defeat the Burgundians and besiege and conquer Lugdunum before early January 459, then fine the city. Cliopatria drops the Rhône valley in 459.
461: the capital moves from Geneva to Lyon (infobox 'Lugdunum 461-534').

region.text: Lyon and the Rhône valley, down to the Drôme and the Vaucluse

ledger.note: 462: Lyon and the Rhône valley return to the Burgundians. 'Lyon was taken from imperial control during the later 460s'; the Burgundians pushed south toward the Drôme. The infobox has Lyon as capital from 461, Cliopatria and the western-roman-empire dossier have 462: the page's own dates disagree.

region.text: the Langres-Besançon-Jura march: Maxima Sequanorum around Besançon and the Jura, 'parts of Lugdunensis I' on the Langres side

ledger.note: Mid-470s: the Burgundians push into the Alemannic marches. 'by the mid-470s Burgundians were active against the Alemanni in the Langres-Besançon-Jura region, eventually incorporating much of Maxima Sequanorum and parts of Lugdunensis I into their sphere' (Kingdom page; 'sphere', not a border). Cliopatria's 443 shape already holds this land (the Sapaudia page puts Franche-Comté inside Sapaudia), so the event moves no cell: ledger and keyframes disagree on when it became Burgundian, and the 443 shape is marked 'unverified: page budget' (keyframe 443). After review eu-06-c the region is Besançon 80 km inside the 480 shape (the first version also named Franche-Comté and held 15 cells that no Burgundian shape contains); Langres itself (Haute-Marne) lies outside every Cliopatria Burgundian shape. Confidence 1: the year is 'mid-470s', the land is not new in the keyframes. The kingdom-of-alamannia dossier records no matching loss.

region.text: Dijon, where Gundobad was beaten, and Vienne, Godegisel's seat

ledger.note: 500: Clovis and Godegisel fight Gundobad. Godegisel allied with Clovis I, and Gundobad was defeated in a battle near Dijon, then retreated to Avignon (Kingdom page); Marius of Avenches dates the conflict to 500 and Clovis spared Gundobad for a yearly tribute (Gundobad page).

501: Gundobad retakes Vienne. Gundobad retook Vienne, killing Godegisel and the Frankish garrison; the Gundobad page has him break the tribute promise, enter by the aqueduct and kill Godegisel in an Arian church.

region.text: Gothic Provence beyond the Burgundian frontier of 500, without Arles

ledger.note: 507: after Vouillé the Burgundians take Gothic Provence. After the Battle of Vouillé, the Burgundians took Gothic territory in Provence and raided toward Toulouse and Barcelona (Kingdom page, 507-509); the Vouillé page dates the battle 'around spring 507' and has Narbonne 'taken by Burgundian allies of the Franks'. The page names Provence, not a line. The region leaves out Arles (30 km): the Gundobad page has the Ostrogothic army relieve 'the Burgundian siege of Arles' and the Burgundians losing 'hope of acquiring Arles and Avignon', so Arles was never Burgundian; the visigothic-kingdom dossier keeps Provence to 510 and has no 507 loss to the Burgundians.

region.text: Provence between the Durance and the sea, the Burgundian gains of 507, without Arles

ledger.note: 508: the Ostrogoths enter Provence. The Kingdom page has Ostrogothic intervention in 508-509; the Gundobad page has Ostrogothic forces relieving the Burgundian siege of Arles and devastating as far as Orange, the Burgundians losing their conquered territories and hopes for Arles and Avignon. The region leaves out Arles, which the Burgundians besieged but never took (Gundobad page).

region.text: Provence south of the Durance, without Arles

ledger.note: 509: the fighting ends on the Durance. Ostrogothic intervention in 508-509 stripped these gains, and the Durance was fixed as the southern frontier. The ostrogothic-kingdom dossier dates the Ostrogothic annexation of Provence 510. The region leaves out Arles (never taken, Gundobad page); it is the gazetteer's Provence, wider than the Durance line.

region.text: Provence south of the Durance, without Arles

ledger.note: 509: the Provence gains are lost. The Ostrogoths stripped these gains, fixing the Durance as the southern frontier of the Burgundians. The region leaves out Arles (never taken, Gundobad page); it is the gazetteer's Provence, wider than the Durance line.

Godomar II recovered territory south of the Durance during his reign (524-534, infobox): 'the recovery of territory south of the Durance' (Kingdom page), with no year and no bounds; after the victory of Vézeronce on 25 June 524 the Godomar page has 'With this army, he regained his territory'. 524 is the start of his reign and of that victory. After review eu-06-c the region is a stand-in cut to what the page says: the Provence cells outside the 500 shape and Arles that lie within 20 km of the Durance (31 cells, about 7,800 km2, all inside Cliopatria's Ostrogothic Kingdom 523 shape), not the whole of Provence; keyframe burgundian-kingdom_524 adds the same strip. Conflict between pages: the Ostrogothic Kingdom page says that after the Franks invaded Burgundy in 523 Theodoric 'could only react by expanding his domains in the Provence north of the river Durance up to the Isère', the opposite bank, while Cliopatria's Burgundian 523 shape holds the Drôme, Isère and Hautes-Alpes to 534. The Tuluin page (Ostrogothic occupation of 523) did not load. Nothing is dated or bounded, so no occupation event is written. The ostrogothic-kingdom dossier holds Provence 510-540 and has no matching loss.

532: the Franks invade again. 'When the Franks made another attempt at conquest in 532, Godomar II was unable to repel them' (Godomar page); the Kingdom page has a coordinated Frankish campaign 532-534 ending in defeat near Autun. The zone around Autun is my reading.
534: the Burgundians are beaten near Autun. The infobox gives the Battle of Autun as 534, with Childebert I and Chlothar I.

region.text: the whole kingdom, divided among the Frankish kings

ledger.note: 534: the Franks end the Burgundian kingdom. 'The rule of the Burgundian kings ended and the kingdom became part of Francia', 'partitioned among the victors, becoming a Frankish sub-kingdom while retaining a distinct Burgundian identity'; the Francia page lists 'Burgundes (534)' among the peoples incorporated under Clovis's sons.

wars.name: Destruction of the Rhine kingdom by Aetius and the Huns
wars.outcome: Gundahar and many of his people were killed by Aetius working with his Hun allies; the survivors were settled in Sapaudia in 443.
wars.note: 'About 436' on the Kingdom page; the Huns dossier carries the Hun side.

wars.name: Majorian's Gallic campaign against the Burgundians
wars.outcome: Majorian defeated the Burgundians and besieged and conquered Lugdunum in late 458 or early 459; the city was fined and Sidonius Apollinaris delivered a panegyric in January 459. Lyon was retaken after Majorian's death in 461.
wars.note: The Majorian page gives no exact date for the siege.

wars.name: Burgundian war with the Visigoths on the lower Rhône
wars.outcome: Chilperic repelled a Visigothic move up the lower Rhône; no border moved.

wars.name: Burgundian campaigns against the Alemanni
wars.outcome: In the mid-470s the Burgundians took much of Maxima Sequanorum and parts of Lugdunensis I from the Alemanni.
wars.note: 'Mid-470s' is the page's phrase; the years 474-476 are my span.

wars.name: Burgundian invasion of Liguria
wars.outcome: While Odoacer and Theoderic fought over Pavia the Burgundians invaded northwestern Italy and devastated Liguria; no land was kept.

wars.name: Burgundian civil war and Clovis's intervention
wars.outcome: Gundobad lost near Dijon, fled to Avignon and was spared by Clovis for a yearly tribute; in 501 he besieged and killed Godegisel at Vienne and ended the tribute.
wars.note: Marius of Avenches dates the conflict to 500 (Gundobad page); the Kingdom page names the battle near Dijon.

wars.name: Burgundian expansion in Provence and the Ostrogothic counter-offensive
wars.outcome: After Vouillé the Burgundians took Gothic land in Provence and besieged Arles; Ostrogothic forces relieved Arles and stripped the gains; the Durance became the southern frontier. Arles is outside the zone: it was besieged and never taken.
wars.note: The Gundobad page does not date the Provence episode; the Vouillé page has only the battle (spring 507).

wars.name: Frankish-Burgundian war of 523-524
wars.outcome: Sigismund was captured and executed; his brother Godomar II defeated the Franks at Vézeronce on 25 June 524 ('On June 25, 524').
wars.note: The Godomar page gives no date for Sigismund's execution; Sigeric's murder is 523.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Burgundy
wars.outcome: Godomar II could not repel the Franks; the defeat near Autun (534, Childebert I and Chlothar I) ended the kingdom, which the Franks divided among themselves.

certainty.note: The pages name cities, provinces and peoples (Worms, Sapaudia, Lyon, the Drôme, Provence), never a surveyed line. The only fixed frontier is the Durance in the south after 509, set by Ostrogothic intervention rather than by treaty, and it is soft here too.

notes:
Page budget: nine pages for 17 shapes; ten were opened (the Sapaudia page, the tenth, adds nothing dated and was spent for the land of 443). Four of them (Francia, Theuderic II, Chlothar II, Clovis II) also serve the sibling dossier frankish-burgundy.

SPLIT OF THE ROW. Cliopatria's 'Burgundian Kingdom' (414-660) is two states: the Kingdom of the Burgundians (413-534: Worms, Sapaudia, Lyon) and the Frankish sub-kingdom of Burgundy (shapes 602-660: the realm of Theuderic II with Aquitaine and the Seine-Loire, then Neustria and Burgundy under Clovis II). This dossier reviews only the 13 shapes 414-523; the 4 later shapes (602, 612, 644, 656) are reviewed in frankish-burgundy.json (a new slug, to be seeded by the colour agent). Validation prints a 'no verdict' warning for those four because both files carry the Name; that is expected.

SAME PEOPLE AS 'burgundians'. Cliopatria's 'Burgundians' (154-409) and this row share Wikidata Q13590051. They are kept as two states: the burgundians dossier ends in 413 with the foederati grant and names this slug as successor; this one starts in 413. The orchestrator may merge the two under 'burgundians' if it prefers one colour for the people.

Cliopatria shapes corrected: (1) 414 holds only to 436 and the shape of 437-438 is dropped (Aetius, c. 436). (2) 455: the Rhône valley starts in 456. (3) 458: Majorian's conquest of Lyon is in 458 (late), so the 459 outline is applied one year earlier. (4) 523 runs to 534. (5) new keyframes 413 (the settlement a year before the row) and 507-508 (Provence after Vouillé).

Not settled: (a) Lyon's return: infobox capital 461, body 'later 460s', Cliopatria and western-roman-empire 462; (b) the 443 shape already holds Côte-d'Or, Nièvre and Yonne although the mid-470s campaign against the Alemanni is when the page has the Burgundians take parts of Lugdunensis I; (c) the twelve Côte-d'Or cells that drop in 462 and the single-cell changes of 469-523, which no page explains; (d) who held Worms after c. 436; (e) the recovery of territory south of the Durance under Godomar (ledger 524, confidence 1); (f) the 474 division of the kingdom among Gundobad, Godegisel, Chilperic II and Godomar I is a division of rule, not of territory, on the pages (seats at Lyon, Geneva, Vienne and Valence); (g) the infobox gives no area, so the 120,000 km2 plateau of 462-533 is unverified against a page.

Counterparts needing matching events in other dossiers: western-roman-empire (413, 436, 443, 456, 458 gain of Lyon, 462), kingdom-of-alamannia (mid-470s), kingdom-of-the-franks (500-501, 532-534, 534), visigothic-kingdom (507 loss of Provence) and ostrogothic-kingdom (508-509; its dossier has the annexation of Provence in 510). The huns dossier has no entry for the c. 436 destruction.

Gazetteer: all region names used (Provence, Franche-Comté, Dijon, Vienne, Besançon, admin-1 units) are in the gazetteer.
